resolutions.resolution: reaffirming previous resolution that the ideal algorithm should be non-normative
resolutions.background: Blink launched an implementation of the specified intrinsic sizing algorithm on Canary for a few days. It was quite clear that the [algorithm for computing the intrinsic main size for single-line row flexboxes](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-flexbox/#intrinsic-main-sizes) is not web compatible. `min-content` sizes are too big. Not yet sure about `max-content` sizes.
irc: <JoshT> oriol: the flexbox spec had an algorithm for intrinsic sizing that was not web compat
<JoshT> ... no major browser was following it
<JoshT> ... now the spec has been changed and has two algirithms. the ideal algorithm and the web compat one that chrome does
<JoshT> ... spec says the implementations must choose one of them
<JoshT> ... but I don't see the point having both if we know one is not web compat
<JoshT> ... we didn't know that the spec was wrong and that browsers were doing something else
<JoshT> ... and having two makes testing more complicated
<JoshT> I don't think that will be useful. I would like to have tests passing
<JoshT> ... other than that, I don't think the ideal algorithm is ideal
<JoshT> ... we still have several reports complaining that different test cases were behaving in unexpected ways
<JoshT> ... like with nested boxes and the auto min size
<JoshT> ... the outcome can be text is forced to overflow instead of break lines which is not idea
<JoshT> ... so I propose we drop the other algorithm
<astearns> ack fantasai
<JoshT> fantasai: for a while we haven't addressed the issue of it not compat
<JoshT> ... now they are both in the spec and there is a note explaining
<JoshT> ... we left it in because we wanted to make it closer to the ideal behaviour if we could
<JoshT> ... we welcomed experimentation on it
<JoshT> ... it's called ideal because the def of max content is when you choose a size where nothing is wrapping or overflowing
<JoshT> ... the current algo don't give that result. it causes overflow
<JoshT> ... i don't understand what's happening in the test case you linked to
<JoshT> ... flex box that is block level should be constrained by the block
<JoshT> oriol: it's the auto min size that prevents shrinking
<JoshT> ... otherwise it's the same as min content. but if it uses the flex basis and that behaves as max content, then that will prevent line breaks
<JoshT> fantasai: it should be using the min size unless the item is inflexible
<JoshT> oriol: if you're requesting min content size, if you have a nested flex box and content behaves as max content, i went into the details and it was something on those lines
<JoshT> fantasai: the result in servo in this case is wrong
<JoshT> ... i don't think the spec would have wanted the result you're describing
<JoshT> oriol: what you are saying about having to ask browsers to experiment, maybe we could have that as a non-normative section but right now require the web compat algorithm
<JoshT> fantasai: there was a time when we only had the non compat algorithm.
<JoshT> ... i agree the test should either fail or pass and organising WPT to target a specific algo
<JoshT> ... in terms of the spec, i would be OK with moving it to an appendix if that would help
<JoshT> astearns: from my reading from the resolution for 3 years ago, the ideal algorithm was meant to be informative
<JoshT> ... but now we have two in the spec
<JoshT> ... we could just reapply the resolution from three years ago
<JoshT> ... maybe open a separate issue on how to get the web compat algorithm not to overflow in the cases where it does
<JoshT> PROPOSED: the ideal algorithm should be non-normative
<JoshT> RESOLVED: reaffirming previous resolution that the ideal algorithm should be non-normative

fresh.title: [cssom] CSSOM serialization of declaration blocks is incompatible across browsers and a forward-compat landmine
fresh.background: ["Serialize a CSS declaration block"](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#serialize-a-css-declaration-block) attempts to consolidate longhand declarations into shorthands for serialization. For example, if you write `justify-self: start; align-self: start;`, this algorithm specifies that they are serialized as `place-self: start;`.

fresh.title: [css-sizing-3][css-sizing-4] Swap levels of fit-content and fit-content()
fresh.background: The `fit-content` keyword, which everyone supports, is in Level 4; whereas the `fit-content()` function, which no one does, is in Level 3.
